messages:
Jordan (Acme): Hey team — we found one of our Redwood API keys in our Logstash index. Looks like one pipeline shipped logs to a public S3. Need urgent rotation + audit. Example log line: `api_key=sk_live_...` in /var/log/logstash/messages-2026-03-15.log. Can you advise next steps? (we already paused that pipeline)

Maya: Thanks @Jordan — sorry this happened. First step: rotate the key immediately and revoke the leaked key. I can trigger rotation if you want, or we can provide steps for you.

Jordan (Acme): Please send steps, we'll do it. Need confirmation we didn't have data exfil via API calls.

Samir: @Jordan — we can help check audit logs. Please DM the exact key id (do NOT paste the full key in-channel). We'll search for recent requests and IPs. Also confirm S3 path + retention window.

Jordan (Acme): DM sent with key id: key_02a8...

Samir: Got it. Running lookups now.

audit-bot: export started for key key_02a8... — job id export-8792. ETA ~6m.

Alex: Action items for Jordan: 1) Revoke leaked key 2) Create new key with least privileges 3) Update apps to use rotated key 4) Purge logs and redact future logs. See snippet below to revoke and rotate quickly:

``
# Revoke via API
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/keys/key_02a8.../revoke" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SUPPORT_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reason":"exposed in external logs"}'

# Or using CLI
redwood keys revoke key_02a8... --reason "leaked in logstash"
``

Maya: After revoke, create a new key and roll out to staging first. For mobile/web SDKs consider short-lived tokens. Also set up environment variable injection instead of baking keys into images.

Samir: We're also checking for suspicious request patterns. If there were any unauthorized requests, we recommend rotating any downstream credentials that could be affected (webhooks, downstream services). We'll attach a short report when audit export finishes.

Jordan (Acme): On S3: `s3://acme-logs/public_dump/2026-03-15/` — we already set bucket to private and started lifecycle to delete. How should we handle log redaction? Need a permanent fix for Logstash.

Maya: For Logstash, add a mutate filter to remove/obfuscate keys before output. Example:

``
filter {
  mutate {
    gsub => [ "message", "(?i)api_key=\S+", "api_key=[REDACTED]" ]
  }
}
``

Also update pipeline to use KMS envelope encryption on the output plugin, and restrict S3 ACLs.

Samir: Recommend also: 1) enable key usage alerts in Console (alerts for any key usage from unusual IPs) 2) enforce rotation via policies 3) store secrets in KMS/HSM and reference them at runtime rather than committing them to config files.

Alex: To check audit logs via API (example):

``
# query events for key
curl "https://api.redwood.com/v1/audit/events?filter=key:key_02a8...&range=24h" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <READ_AUDIT_TOKEN>"
``

Samir: Export complete. No anomalous large-volume writes. There were ~7 requests from two IPs over a 2h window; timestamps match your dev deploy. We'll attach export-8792.zip to this thread and send via secure link.

Jordan (Acme): Thanks — we've revoked and rotated, updated staging and prod, and purged S3. Can you confirm audit log shows no exfil beyond those 7 calls?

Samir: Confirmed — no further activity after rotation. We'll keep monitoring 72h and can re-open if anything shows up.

Maya: I'll follow up with a short checklist and a recommended Logstash config to prevent recurrence. Closing actions: please file a short postmortem and let us know if you want help changing retention or enabling HSM-backed key storage. :lock: :white_check_mark:

Jordan (Acme): Appreciate it — will do postmortem and reach out if we need HSM help. :pray:
